_about: Decisions from reviewing the saints whose date neither the calendar, Wikidata nor the Wikipedia infobox confirmed (18 November 2026), by Claude with a Codex second opinion (first from Codex's memory, then a Codex web search that confirmed one decision and found no source for most). The strongest source used is the Vatican's martyr list (Pontifical Academy Cultorum Martyrum), which covers martyrs only. Every move or relink rests on the evidence quoted; where Codex's view rested only on its own memory, the sourced date was used and Codex's view is recorded. Applied by Scripts/build_saints.py. The app shows each saint's celebrated day; a Martyrology day that differs is shown on the card, never used to move the saint.

decisions.name: The Eternal Father
decisions.evidence: Not in the current General Roman or US proper calendar (Scripts/saint_calendar.json). Wikipedia: "God the Father is a title given to God in Christianity"; not a saint and not a liturgical feast in the calendar.

decisions.name: The Circumcision of Our Lord
decisions.evidence: USCCB (https://www.usccb.org/prayer-and-worship/liturgical-year/christmas/christmas-january-1): 1 January is the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God, already on the calendar.

decisions.codex: Codex: move to 02-12 as the Hospitaller

decisions.name: Canute
decisions.evidence: The entry describes Canute IV, King of Denmark (it linked Cnut the Great). The Vatican's martyr list (https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_academies/cult-martyrum/martiri/009.html) has him on 10 July: "A Odense, in Danimarca, ricordo di S. Canuto (Knut), martire, che, re..."; his infobox also gives 10 July. (19 January is the pre-1969 date; Canute Lavard, a different saint, is 7 January.)
decisions.codex: Codex: keep 01-19 (own knowledge, medium); Codex's web check cited the Vatican list for Canute Lavard (7 January), a different saint

decisions.name: Liberatus

The Vatican's martyr list (https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_academies/cult-martyrum/martiri/009.html) has them on 2 July, not 17 August: "A Cartagine, ricordo dei SS. martiri Liberato, abate, Bonifacio, diacono...". Left out: no Wikipedia article to describe them.

decisions.name: Anacletus
decisions.evidence: The same pope as Cletus (both entries link the Wikipedia article Pope Anacletus); the 2004 Martyrology has one entry, "Cletus Pp, 26 apr., 1 (88)", and the app keeps him on 26 April. 13 July was the pre-1960 separate feast of Anacletus.

decisions.name: Simon
decisions.evidence: Simon of Trent: his death was used as a blood libel against the Jews of Trent, and "on 28 October 1965 ... archbishop of Trent Alessandro Maria Gottardi abolished the cult of Simon" (Wikipedia, Simon of Trent). He is not in the 2004 Martyrology's index of names.

decisions.name: Philomena
decisions.evidence: Not in the 2004 Martyrology's index of names; her Wikipedia article says she was "never formally canonized in the Catholic Church". Removed at Craig's decision (18 November 2026).

decisions.name: Thecla
decisions.evidence: Thecla of Iconium is not in the 2004 Martyrology (its only Thecla is the abbess of Kitzingen, 15 October). Removed at Craig's decision (19 November 2026), as Philomena was.
